title: SCIRIGOR:Evaluating Open-Ended Scientific Analysis Beyond Final Scores
abstract: arXiv:2609.06192v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Scientific coding agents produce interdependent code, results, figures, and claims, yet evaluating final   outputs alone does not establish whether their conclusions are scientifically supported. We formulate   evidence-grounded multimodal scientific analysis, requiring agents to produce executable analyses and claims   supported by results and visualizations from the same run. We introduce SciRIGOR, an evaluation framework and   benchmark comprising 100 cases from scientific articles across six domains and 17 subfields. The framework   reconstructs typed evidence graphs, separates artifact fidelity from relational validity, and scores complete   claim-support paths while localizing the earliest unsupported relation. Source-grounded alternative paths   accommodate scientifically equivalent analyses and visualizations. We evaluate 11 agent/model configurations. translated_title: SCIRIGOR：超越最终分数的开放式科学分析评估
translated_abstract: 科学编码智能体会产生相互依赖的代码、结果、图表和论断，然而仅评估最终输出并不能确定其结论是否得到了科学支持。我们提出了证据支撑的多模态科学分析这一任务，要求智能体生成可执行的分析，以及由同一次运行所产生的结果和可视化所支撑的论断。我们介绍了SciRIGOR，这是一个评估框架和基准，包含来自六个领域、17个子领域的科学文章中的100个案例。该框架重建类型化的证据图，将产物保真度与关系有效性分离开来，对完整的论断-支撑路径进行评分，同时定位出最早出现的不受支撑的关联。基于原始来源的备选路径可以容纳科学上等价的分析和可视化方案。我们评估了11种智能体/模型配置。在完整基准的运行中，论断与忠实及不忠实结果的…
tldr: SciRIGOR提出了一个新的评估框架和基准，通过重建证据图来检验科学编码智能体的论断是否真正得到同一次运行中结果与可视化的支持，从而超越仅看最终分数的传统评估方式。
en_tdlr: SciRIGOR is an evaluation framework and benchmark that verifies whether scientific coding agents' claims are genuinely supported by results and visualizations from the same run, using reconstructed evidence graphs rather than final scores alone.
